rows.stem: Choose the correct option that indicates the enzyme, ribozyme in bacteria that acts as a catalyst.
rows.solution: During translation the ribosome does more than hold the mRNA and tRNAs in place: it also catalyses the formation of **peptide bonds** between amino acids. In bacteria this catalytic activity belongs to an RNA, the **23S rRNA** of the large ribosomal subunit, so it is an RNA enzyme or **ribozyme**. The 28S and \(5{\cdot}8\)S rRNAs are found in the large subunit of eukaryotic ribosomes, not in bacteria. So the answer is option (D) 23S rRNA.

rows.stem: When a pure tall pea plant (Pisum sativum) with green pod is crossed with dwarf pea plant with yellow pod, how many dwarf pea plants, out of 16, will be produced in \(\text{F}_2\) generation ?
rows.solution:
Tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t) and green pod (G) is dominant over yellow pod (g), so the cross is TTGG \(\times\) ttgg.
- The \(\text{F}_1\) plants are all TtGg (tall, green pod).
- Selfing the \(\text{F}_1\) gives the dihybrid ratio 9 tall green : 3 tall yellow : 3 dwarf green : 1 dwarf yellow in the \(\text{F}_2\).
- The dwarf plants are the 3 dwarf green plus the 1 dwarf yellow, that is 4 out of 16.

This is also the monohybrid 3 : 1 ratio for height (12 tall : 4 dwarf), because the two genes assort independently. So the answer is option (C) 4.

options.label: B

rows.stem:
Inheritance of which of the following traits is shown in the cross given below ?
XY (Normal man) and \(\text{XX}^{\text{C}}\) (Carrier woman)
\(\downarrow\)
\(\text{XX}^{\text{C}}\) (Carrier daughter), XX (Normal daughter), XY (Normal son), \(\text{X}^{\text{C}}\text{Y}\) Genetic disorders (Diseased son)
Choose the correct option from the following :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE: a cross diagram of labels only: the parents XY (Normal man) and XX^C (Carrier woman) joined by a horizontal line, from which a vertical line branches into four arrows down to the offspring XX^C (Carrier daughter), XX (Normal daughter), XY (Normal son) and X^CY Genetic disorders (Diseased son). Every label is carried in the stem as text lines (the stem joins the parents with 'and' where the drawing has a line), so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
The mother is a carrier (\(\text{XX}^{\text{C}}\)) and the father is normal (XY). Her two X chromosomes pass in equal proportion to the children:
- daughters receive the father's normal X, so they are either normal (XX) or carriers (\(\text{XX}^{\text{C}}\)), never affected;
- sons receive their only X from the mother, so half are normal (XY) and half are affected (\(\text{X}^{\text{C}}\text{Y}\)).

The trait is carried on the X chromosome, a single copy shows the disorder only in males (who have no second X to mask it), and a heterozygous female is an unaffected carrier. This is **X-linked recessive** inheritance, as in haemophilia and colour blindness. So the answer is option (C) X-linked recessive trait.

rows.stem:
Given below are few statements with reference to the human male reproductive system.
(i) Paired seminal vesicles, prostate gland and bulbourethral gland constitute the male accessory glands.
(ii) Secretions of the male accessory glands constitute the seminal plasma.
(iii) Secretions of the bulbourethral glands help in the lubrication of the penis.
(iv) Enlarged end of the the penis is known as foreskin.
(v) Seminal plasma is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes.
Choose the option with all true statements from the given options :
rows.solution:
- (i) Not accepted as worded: the male accessory glands are the **paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands**; the statement makes the bulbourethral gland a single gland.
- (ii) True: the secretions of the male accessory glands constitute the **seminal plasma**.
- (iii) True: the secretions of the **bulbourethral glands** also help in the lubrication of the penis.
- (iv) False: the enlarged end of the penis is the **glans penis**; the foreskin is the loose fold of skin that covers it.
- (v) True: seminal plasma is rich in **fructose, calcium and certain enzymes**.

Every other choice contains the false statement (iv), and only (ii), (iii) and (v) are all true, which is option (B) (ii), (iii) and (v).

rows.stem: If a natural population of 60 individuals is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with two alleles B and b, with the gene frequency of allele B of \(0{\cdot}7\), the genotype frequency of Bb will be :
rows.solution:
For a gene with two alleles, let p be the frequency of B and q the frequency of b.
- p = \(0{\cdot}7\), so q = \(1 - 0{\cdot}7 = 0{\cdot}3\).
- At Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium the genotype frequencies are \(p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1\), and the heterozygote Bb has frequency \(2pq\).
- \(2pq = 2 \times 0{\cdot}7 \times 0{\cdot}3 = 0{\cdot}42\).

The population size (60 individuals) does not enter the calculation. So the answer is option (B) \(0{\cdot}42\).

rows.stem: In a DNA, the percentage of thymine is 20. What is the percentage of guanine in it ?
rows.solution:
By **Chargaff's rule**, in double-stranded DNA adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine, so A = T and G = C.
- Thymine is 20%, so adenine is also 20%, and A + T = 40%.
- The remaining 60% is G + C, shared equally, so guanine = 30% (and cytosine = 30%).

So the answer is option (C) 30%.

rows.stem:
Select the statements that are true for embryo of the flowering plants from the given options.
(i) The zygote forms a proembryo and subsequently heart-shaped, globular and mature embryo.
(ii) Most zygotes divide to form embryo only after a certain amount of endosperm is formed.
(iii) The embryo develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac.
(iv) A typical dicotyledonous embryo consists of an embryonal axis and a scutellum.
Choose the correct option from the following :
rows.solution:
- (i) False: the zygote gives rise to the proembryo, and then to the **globular**, **heart-shaped** and mature embryo, in that order; the statement puts heart-shaped before globular.
- (ii) True: most zygotes divide only after a certain amount of **endosperm** has formed, since the endosperm provides nutrition to the developing embryo.
- (iii) True: the embryo develops at the **micropylar end** of the embryo sac, where the zygote is situated.
- (iv) False: a typical dicotyledonous embryo consists of an embryonal axis and **two cotyledons**; the **scutellum** is the single cotyledon of a grass (monocot) embryo.

So the true statements are (ii) and (iii), which is option (B) (ii) and (iii).

rows.stem: Human Immunodeficiency Virus is a member of the group of viruses known as :
rows.solution: HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, has an **RNA genome**. After it enters a host cell such as a macrophage, its RNA is copied into viral DNA by the enzyme **reverse transcriptase**, and this DNA is incorporated into the host cell's DNA. Viruses that copy RNA into DNA in this way, reversing the usual direction of information flow, are called **retroviruses**. So the answer is option (B) Retrovirus.

rows.stem: The animals that evolved into the first amphibians during evolutionary history were :
rows.solution:
About 350 million years ago, fish with stout and strong fins, the **lobefins**, could move on land and go back to water. In 1938 a fish caught in South Africa turned out to be a **Coelacanth**, a lobefin that was thought to be extinct. NCERT records that these animals, the lobefins (the Coelacanth being the living example), evolved into the **first amphibians**, which lived on both land and water. The marking scheme takes the Coelacanth as the answer.

Archaeopteryx is the fossil link between reptiles and birds, and the salamander is itself an amphibian, not the ancestor of amphibians. So the answer is option (C) Coelacanth.

rows.stem: The cloning site present in the rop site of E. coli cloning vector pBR322 is :
Bacteria growing anaerobically on cellulosic material produce large amounts of which gases ? Select the correct option.
rows.solution:
CBSE awarded this mark to every candidate who attempted the question, because none of the four choices is correct as printed.

Certain bacteria that grow anaerobically on cellulosic material, the **methanogens** (for example Methanobacterium), produce large amounts of **methane (\(\text{CH}_4\))** along with **carbon dioxide (\(\text{CO}_2\)) and hydrogen (\(\text{H}_2\))**. These bacteria are found in the anaerobic sludge of sewage treatment and in the rumen of cattle, and the gas mixture they produce is **biogas**.

The intended answer was evidently methane, carbon dioxide and hydrogen, but the choice that lists carbon dioxide and hydrogen prints \(\text{CH}_3\), a methyl group and not a gas, in place of methane. Of the others, one adds ammonia, one lists water vapour, chlorine and hydrogen sulphide, and one adds oxygen, none of which is the gas mixture of biogas. That is why the Board gave the mark to all.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : In some species of asteraceae and grasses, seeds are formed without fertilization.
Reason (R) : Formation of fruit without fertilization is called parthenocarpy.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is true: in some species of **Asteraceae** and grasses, seeds are formed without fertilisation. This is **apomixis**, a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction; for example, a diploid egg cell may form without reduction division and develop into the embryo without being fertilised.

The Reason is also true: the development of a fruit without fertilisation is called **parthenocarpy**, as in banana, and such fruits are seedless.

But the Reason does not explain the Assertion: apomixis produces seeds without fertilisation, while parthenocarpy produces fruits (usually without seeds) without fertilisation. So both statements are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
Answer the following questions with respect to the sex determination mechanism in birds :
(a) Name the type of heterogamety observed in most birds.
(b) If the birds have 18 pairs of autosomal chromosomes and a pair of sex chromosomes, fill in the blanks (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) in the table given below. (Use symbols Z and W for sex chromosomes.)
| | Total number of autosomes (in a diploid cell) | Type of sex chromosomes (in a diploid cell) |
|---|---|---|
| Male bird | (i) ______ | (ii) ______ |
| Female bird | (iii) ______ | (iv) ______ |
rows.solution:
(a) Most birds show **female heterogamety**. The female has two different sex chromosomes, **ZW**, and produces two kinds of eggs (with Z or with W), while the male has two similar sex chromosomes, **ZZ**, and produces only one kind of sperm (with Z). So the sex of the chick is decided by the egg, that is, by the female.

(b) The bird has 18 pairs of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes, so a diploid cell of either sex carries \(18 \times 2 = 36\) autosomes and two sex chromosomes.

| | Total number of autosomes (in a diploid cell) | Type of sex chromosomes (in a diploid cell) |
|---|---|---|
| Male bird | (i) 36 | (ii) ZZ |
| Female bird | (iii) 36 | (iv) ZW |

rows.stem:
(i) Describe the approach of gene therapy used for the treatment of a 4-year-old girl suffering from Adenosine Deaminase Deficiency.
(ii) What is meant by microprogation ? Name any two important food plants grown commercially (on a large scale) by this method.
Describe the technique of a typical agarose gel electrophoresis used for the separation and isolation of DNA fragments.
rows.solution:
Agarose gel electrophoresis separates and isolates the DNA fragments obtained by cutting DNA with restriction endonucleases:
- **Principle:** DNA fragments are **negatively charged** molecules, so they can be separated by forcing them to move towards the **anode** under an electric field through a medium or matrix.
- **The matrix:** the commonly used matrix is **agarose**, a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds. The DNA samples are loaded into wells at the cathode end of the gel and the current is switched on.
- **Separation:** the fragments resolve according to their **size** through the **sieving effect** of the agarose gel; the smaller the fragment, the farther it moves.
- **Visualisation:** pure DNA fragments cannot be seen in visible light, so the gel is stained with **ethidium bromide** and exposed to **UV radiation**, when the DNA fragments appear as bright orange coloured bands.
- **Isolation (elution):** the separated bands of DNA are cut out from the agarose gel and extracted from the gel piece. This step is known as **elution**.

The DNA fragments purified in this way are used in constructing recombinant DNA by joining them with cloning vectors.
